_about: Hover texts of the brain diagrams (js/life-book.js): one or two plain sentences per cell, group and modulator, about what it does. Groups by their full path (valence/gates, not gates). Every region, group and modulator of an exported stage needs an entry (tests/test_book.py checks it); see book/README.md.

cells.in: The senses: the eyes (what lies ahead and to the sides), sound, taste, pain, the skin's warmth, the stomach, what the creature holds, and its age.
cells.out: The motor neurons, one per action: wait, step forward, turn left, turn right, use, eat, call. The most active one is carried out.
cells.ganglion_e: Excitatory cells of the ganglion. Their wiring is entirely evolved and none of them has a fixed meaning.
cells.ganglion_i: Inhibitory cells of the ganglion. Their wiring is entirely evolved and none of them has a fixed meaning.
cells.valence_app: The good cells. Taste is wired to them, and they drive the bite. The look of a bush can come to excite them too.
cells.valence_av: The bad cells. Pain is wired to them; they turn the creature away and stop the bite. The look of a bush that hurt before comes to excite them.
cells.no_feed: Driven by the bad cells, it blocks the bite.
cells.no_touch: A gate: it fires whenever nothing is within reach and holds grasp shut.
cells.grasp: When it fires, the creature bites what is in front of it.
cells.us_pain: The pain teacher, driven by pain alone. When it fires, it releases the signal that teaches the synapses onto the bad cells.
cells.us_taste: The taste teacher, driven by taste alone: the good outcome, one of the terms of the surprise.
cells.cold: Fires while the skin is cold.
cells.warm_seek: Driven by cold: keeps the creature stepping forward while it is cold.
cells.rest: Fires while the skin is warm and holds the forward step back, so the creature stays where it is warm or where it settled.
cells.hungry: Fires when the stomach is less than about two-thirds full and shuts warm_seek and rest: a hungry creature forages.
cells.flee: Driven by the modulator alarm: after repeated pain, the creature keeps going forward for a while, out of the poisoned ground.
cells.fed: Fires when the creature tastes food and releases serotonin.
cells.settle: Driven by serotonin: after several good bites it switches on rest, so the creature stays where it ate.
cells.pallium: 128 cells, each reading the colours seen straight ahead through random synapses. Only the two most driven fire, so look-alike bushes activate different cells.
cells.value_app: Predicts how good the next few moments will be for what the creature sees; learned within the life from the surprise.
cells.value_av: Predicts how bad the next few moments will be for what the creature sees; learned within the life from the surprise.
cells.value_app_prev: A copy of value_app one tick ago: the prediction a moment ago, one of the terms of the surprise.
cells.value_av_prev: A copy of value_av one tick ago: the prediction a moment ago, one of the terms of the surprise.
cells.dopamine: The dopamine cell: it fires at a steady resting rate; a burst above it means better than expected, a pause below it worse. Its rate minus the rest is the surprise that teaches.
cells.habenula: Carries bad news to the dopamine cell: pain excites it, and it silences dopamine. A predicted pain holds it down, so a pain that fails to come makes dopamine burst.
cells.ventral_pallidum: A steadily active cell that holds the dopamine cell back; the cells that predict good things inhibit it, so a rising good prediction releases dopamine at once (the fast path).
cells.gp_habenular: A steadily active cell of the pallidum that holds the habenula back; the cells that predict bad things inhibit it, so a rising bad prediction excites the habenula and pauses dopamine (the fast path).
cells.no_hold: A gate cell that fires while the hand is empty and holds the eating programme shut: nothing to swallow.
cells.ingest: The eating programme: it swallows what is held unless aversion stops it, the more readily the better the held thing looks.
cells.striatum_d1: Go cells of the dorsal striatum, one per hand action (use, eat). Dopamine bursts strengthen their input from the situation in which the action was taken; they release that action.
cells.striatum_d2: NoGo cells of the dorsal striatum, one per hand action. Dopamine dips strengthen their input from the situation in which the action was taken; they hold that action back.
cells.gpe: The outer pallidum: tonically active cells that the NoGo cells silence, which frees the inner pallidum to hold an action back.
cells.gpi: The inner pallidum, the basal ganglia's output: tonically active cells that hold each hand action shut until the Go cells silence them.
cells.act: The hand actions (use, eat) as the basal ganglia release them: shut while the inner pallidum is active, firing when it is silenced.
cells.no_eat: A gate cell driven by aversion to what is held: it stops the eating programme, so a held thing that is known to be bad is not swallowed.

groups.ganglion: A small net of evolved cells between the senses and the motor neurons: the first brain, like the nerve cords of a worm.
groups.valence: Good and bad: cells whose meaning is fixed by their wiring to taste and pain, and the cells through which they act on biting.
groups.valence/gates: Cells that hold an action shut until it can be done.
groups.valence/programmes: Cells that run one action when they fire.
groups.us: The teachers: cells driven by something that matters without any learning (pain, taste). US stands for unconditioned stimulus.
groups.hypothalamus: The body's needs: cells that read the stomach and the skin's warmth and switch behaviour between foraging and staying warm.
groups.affect: Lasting states built up by modulators: alarm after repeated pain, contentment after good meals.
groups.forebrain: The front of the brain, where what is seen is learned about within a life.
groups.forebrain/pallium: The roof of the forebrain; in mammals most of it became the cerebral cortex.
groups.forebrain/basal_ganglia: The critic: cells that learn to predict good and bad outcomes, and whose change of prediction is part of the surprise that dopamine signals.
groups.epithalamus: Above the thalamus: the habenula, a relay of bad news to the dopamine cells.
groups.midbrain: The midbrain: here the cells that broadcast dopamine.
groups.midbrain/dopamine: The dopamine cells of the midbrain (VTA and substantia nigra), which report surprise to the whole forebrain.
groups.forebrain/basal_ganglia/ventral_striatum: The ventral striatum (nucleus accumbens): inhibitory cells that learn from the pallium what a sight predicts, and report it to the dopamine cells slowly (directly) and fast (through the pallidum).
groups.forebrain/basal_ganglia/pallidum: The pallidum: steadily active cells through which the striatum acts, by inhibiting them.
groups.forebrain/basal_ganglia/dorsal_striatum: The dorsal striatum: the actor. It learns which action pays in which situation and releases or holds back the actions through the pallidum.

modulators.us_av: The pain teacher's signal: it lets the synapses onto the bad cells grow.
modulators.us_app: The taste teacher's signal: it lets the synapses onto the good cells grow.
modulators.alarm: Released by pain and cleared slowly: a running sum of recent pain that drives flee.
modulators.serotonin: Released by fed and cleared slowly: a running sum of recent good bites that drives settle.
modulators.da: Dopamine, the surprise: taste minus pain, plus the prediction now, minus the prediction a moment ago. In the critic built from cells it is the dopamine cell's rate minus its rest. It teaches the value cells.
modulators.da_neg: The same surprise with its sign turned round, for the synapses onto the bad cells: a bad surprise strengthens the aversion, a good one weakens it.
